chunks: And with this chain of narration, he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:

Beware of denying Allah. It was said: O Messenger of Allah, and how is that? He said: One of you says: Allah said, so Allah says: You lied, I did not say it. Or he says: Allah did not say, so Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: You lied, I have indeed said it.
ai.seo_question: How does one know if they are falsely attributing a statement to Allah?
ai.summary: In *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith to emphasize the precision required in *tawatur* (mass transmission) and the danger of *ghuluw* (exaggeration) or negligence when attributing divine speech. This warning underscores the theological principle that the Prophet’s role as a trustworthy transmitter (*al-Amiin*) requires strict fidelity to the Divine Message, ensuring that religious rulings and beliefs are not distorted by human error. It serves as a critical guideline for scholars in verifying the authenticity of narrations before establishing them as binding religious truths.
